findings.title: add_members/remove_member require params[:group_id] but the routes only supply params[:id]
findings.body: The new routes in config/routes.rb are declared directly inside the `resources :groups` block (`put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`), which makes them member routes: the URL is `/admin/groups/:id/members` and the group id arrives as `params[:id]`. Both actions call `params.require(:group_id)`, which raises `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (rendered as a 400) on every real request, so adding or removing members from the admin UI is completely broken. The specs pass only because rspec controller specs bypass routing and inject `group_id` directly into the params hash. The controller should read `params[:id]` (or the routes should be changed to actually provide `:group_id`).

findings.title: totalPages off-by-one shows an extra empty page when user_count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. For a group whose member count is an exact multiple of the page size (e.g. 100 members with limit 50) this yields 3 pages even though only 2 exist. The admin can then click "next" from page 2 (showingLast is false), which sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` = 100, and `findMembers` fetches offset 100 from the server, landing on a permanently empty page 3. The computation should be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and the next-page clamp should not allow offset == user_count.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncates non-automatic groups to 50 members with no way to see more
findings.body: Previously `members` returned every member of a non-automatic group (only automatic groups were paginated). Now `.limit(limit).offset(offset)` is applied unconditionally with a default limit of 50, but the public template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` has no pagination controls — it just iterates `members` once. Any group with more than 50 members (a common case, and the reason the old code had a workaround for the 200-member truncation bug) will only ever display the first 50 members alphabetically, with no UI to access the rest.

findings.title: Adding a user who is already a member raises a unique-violation 500
findings.body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` for every username found, with no check for existing membership. `Group#add` does `self.users << user`, which immediately inserts a `group_users` row; the join table has a unique index on (group_id, user_id), so re-adding an existing member raises `PG::UniqueViolation`/`ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` and returns a 500 to the admin. This is easy to hit from the UI because the `addMembers` controller action deliberately does not clear the usernames input (see the TODO in admin-group.js.es6), so clicking "Add" a second time re-submits the same usernames. Duplicates should be skipped (e.g. `group.users.include?(user)` or rescue/ignore the conflict).

findings.title: No upper bound on the limit parameter of the public members endpoint
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` accepts any client-supplied value, so `GET /groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` will serialize and return every member of the group in a single request. This endpoint is visible to anyone who can see the group, so an unbounded limit is an easy way to force expensive queries and huge responses. The limit should be clamped to a sane maximum (e.g. 50–200).

findings.title: add_members doesn't strip whitespace when splitting usernames
findings.body: `usernames.split(",").each` looks up each entry verbatim. If the input contains spaces after commas ("alice, bob"), the lookup `User.find_by_username(" bob")` fails and that user is silently skipped while the response still reports success. Each username should be stripped before lookup.

findings.title: `{{#unless automatic}}` in the member item view never sees the group's automatic flag
findings.body: This template is rendered as an itemView for each member, so its context is the member user, not the admin group controller. `automatic` is not a property of the user, so the `{{#unless automatic}}` guard always passes and the remove (×) link is rendered even for automatic groups. Clicking it then fires `removeMember`, which the server rejects with a 422. The automatic check needs to be passed through explicitly (e.g. via the view) instead of relying on context lookup.

findings.title: Member endpoint specs use the wrong verb and bypass routing, hiding the broken route params
findings.body: The "cannot remove members from automatic groups" test issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the actual route is `delete /admin/groups/:id/members`. More generally, both new endpoint specs pass `group_id` directly in the params, so they exercise the action in a way no real request can: the member routes deliver the group id as `params[:id]`, meaning `params.require(:group_id)` in the controller fails in production while the specs stay green. These should be request/integration specs that go through the router, using the correct DELETE/PUT verbs and URLs.
